active_discriminator: Whether a uniform bound on finite I (or the stronger small L^3 critical velocity control used to certify finite I) can by itself force a universal uniform-in-time global L^{3/2,infinity} vorticity bound on the same forward slab.

candidate_falsifier.construction_family: compactly supported oscillatory vector-potential data with N-independent small L^3 velocity and N-growing initial vorticity
candidate_falsifier.fail_condition: If exact small-data Navier-Stokes dynamics plus the source-bound finite-I implication do not give a uniform finite-I ledger, or if the weak-Lorentz vorticity lower bound does not persist for positive times, prune the calibration itself.
candidate_falsifier.success_scope: Refutes only a universal same-slab finite-I/critical-velocity-to-vorticity-amplitude producer bound with no extra history/frequency/profile assumptions.

difference_witnesses: calibration solutions are globally regular small-data solutions, not candidate singular solutions
large vorticity is injected at the left temporal edge, not proved to arise near a first singular terminal time
Grujic critical-point profile and phase assumptions are absent
longer one-sided history, spectral/frequency envelope, no-recrossing, or singularity-persistence information may add excluded structure

primary_sources.source: Albritton-Barker, arXiv:1811.00502v2 / J. Math. Fluid Mech. 21 (2019) 43
primary_sources.use: definition of I; weak Serrin/critical velocity control implies finite I

problem_signature: whole-space R3, viscosity normalized to 1, smooth rapidly decaying divergence-free data
producer ledger: same-slab critical velocity control / Albritton-Barker finite I
consumer amplitude: global uniform-in-time vorticity L^{3/2,infinity}
counterexample-first exact Navier-Stokes calibration; no numerical theorem authority
separate local producer failure from global/far-field and pre-singularity/ancient gluing

root_contract.target: Clay statement A, whole-space unforced 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes

structural_coordinates: Navier-Stokes scaling u_lambda=lambda u(lambda x,lambda^2 t), omega_lambda=lambda^2 omega(lambda x,lambda^2 t)
L^3 velocity and L^{3/2,infinity} vorticity are scale-critical but differ by one spatial derivative
finite I consists of scale-invariant local energy/cubic/pressure/dissipation spacetime quantities, not an endpoint time-trace derivative norm
a counterexample family must be exact Navier-Stokes, smooth, divergence-free, whole-space, and must keep the critical velocity/finite-I ledger uniformly controlled
temporal-edge high frequency is a DifferenceWitness from first-singular-time profile dynamics and cannot be over-transferred
